topicAssessments.reasoning: Negligible interaction is qualified by the exception for brief collisions. The source kinetic-versus-interaction-energy comparison is retained as an approximate statement about the magnitude of interaction energy with the separated-molecule zero convention, not a coordinate-independent energy-zero assertion or denial of collisions.

Microscopic idealization and macroscopic equation (2-19) remain linked as two descriptions of the ideal model. No claim that real gases obey it exactly in every state. Both source historical equation names remain declared with source-bound reasons; no new history claim.

Ideal approximation requires sufficient dilution and temperature/other conditions limiting interaction effects. Molecular separation, small occupied-volume fraction and approximately free between-collision motion are retained. Short-range repulsion models collisions; the text does not claim real forces materialize only at an instant.

Massive steel-ball analogy remains explicitly a model, not molecular composition. Molecular mass/internal-structure differences and model limitations remain. Pressure prediction is scoped to negligible interaction and approximately elastic collisions; experimental agreement is not universal validation of all molecular processes.

Retains many-particle complexity, source experimental basis, irregular thermal motion, collision-induced possible changes of speed/direction, and collective statistical laws. Irregular individual motion is not equated with absence of dynamics or identical directed velocities.

Direction symmetry explicitly uses equilibrium, isotropy and the gas-rest frame. Equal opposite-direction populations are statistical, not exact counts in every finite snapshot. Unbiased pedestrian analogy and exclusion of directed parades are retained without claiming every street is directionally balanced.

Age arithmetic analogy and finite-sample mean remain, with equilibrium stability qualified. v_i denotes speed relative to the gas, not signed vector velocity. Equation (3-1) averages squared speeds, not the square of the mean. Independent algebra: their difference is the mean of (v_i minus mean speed)^2, nonnegative. n is dimensionless molecular count, not number density; all squared-speed terms have velocity-squared units. No total/internal-energy or mixed-mass equality is introduced.

Orthogonal axes and signed components make (3-2) the squared Euclidean norm identity. The source Pythagorean footnote and name remain. Averaging that identity term-by-term yields (3-3) by linearity, without requiring isotropy, independence or zero correlations.

Isotropy makes the three component second moments equal in (3-4). Substituting into (3-3) gives three times one component, hence (3-5) and factor 1/3. Three dimensions alone do not imply equal shares: paired opposite x-directed velocities can have zero mean flow but unequal component second moments. Text correctly retains the sum identity while excluding the equal-share inference for anisotropic motion.
